Thanks again for the demo today — SpectraWorks is excited to move from the hosted API to a dedicated pool once we hit the next commit. Before we lock dates with Procurement, our infra team asked for two things so they can sign the internal change:

1) A throughput validation that maps our current hosted QPS to the recommended GPU allocation (NVIDIA A100 80GB or equivalent). Our 95th percentile burst is about 420 rps for generation with median seq len 256, and embeddings traffic averages 120 rps.
2) A proposed cutover window and rollback cadence — we need a short blackout, a staged mirror period, and an SLA fallback plan.

Attaching a sample traffic export and our internal SLA template. Can your team provide a concise sizing hypothesis and an acceptance timeline (we're targeting mid-November).

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Folks — did a first-cut pass on the CSV and sketched a few capacity scenarios. Summary up front:

- Baseline assumption: single LLM generation model (ca. 6B dense-ish) + separate embeddings model. Hosted avg latency for generation ~180ms p50, 320ms p95. We assume A100 80GB or H100 equivalent.

Sizing scenarios (short):
1) Conservative (headroom x2): 3 x A100 nodes, each with 160 concurrent streams (small batch) => sustained 450 rps with p95 ~340ms. Good safety margin for 5–10 min bursts.
2) Cost-optimized (headroom x1.2): 2 x A100 nodes, configured with aggressive batching and prefix KV caching => sustained 300 rps, p95 ~360–400ms under sustained load. Not recommended for long 10+ minute spikes.
3) Burst-tiered (recommended operational profile): Primary 2 x A100 for steady-state + 1 warm spare pool (prepped GPUs) that can be brought into rotation within 3–5 minutes for burst coverage. This gives you cost control with predictable burst handling.

Notes on tuning and acceptance tests:
- Batch tuning: simulate your 30/60/90s spike patterns; our runtime will show clear perf curves as we vary batch delay from 5–40ms. I attached a mock perf-curve from a similar deal — it shows the knee where latency jumps with batch size.
- KV prefix cache: enable on dedicated to reduce repeated context cost for conversational flows. Will buy ~20–30% token-cost reduction and lower p95.
- Throughput verification: run a 30-minute staged mirror at 80% of burst (<350 rps) and then 2 x 5-minute burst windows at 420–480 rps. Monitor token queueing, GPU util, and request tail latencies.

Failure/fallback triggers (practical):
- If p95 generation latency > 1s for 3 consecutive minutes => auto-failover to hosted variant for a percentage of traffic (10–30%) as a circuit breaker.
- If GPU OOM or >90% sustained queue depth for 10 min => rollback to hosted entirely and open incident.

Deliverables I’ll push by EOD tomorrow: a perf-curve mock, a staging-run checklist, and a recommended node config.

Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: initial traffic profile and ask — action plan and timeline

Emma — thanks everyone for the fast turnaround. Here’s a concise action plan to unblock Procurement and schedule the cutover: 

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Karthik: deliver formal sizing doc + perf-curve PNG + node config (EOD 2026-11-02) [attached].
- SpectraWorks: confirm whether bursts are 30-90s or sustained (reply by 2026-11-03).
- Marissa: confirm committed units and whether warm-spare will be billable or part of operational buffer (reply 2026-11-04).
- Ben / Sales: confirm cutover financial milestone alignment for Nov 20 cutover (reply 2026-11-03).

Staging & cutover timeline (proposed):
- 2026-11-16 (Tue): staging dry-run — 2 hour mirror at 80% of peak (observability & tracing enabled). Go/no-go checklist executed.
- 2026-11-18 (Thu): short blackout window (2 hours) for final DNS and routing switch tests. Fallback to hosted available immediately.
- 2026-11-20 (Sun) 02:00–06:00 UTC: production cutover window. Post-cutover monitoring run for 72 hours.

Rollback / safety nets:
- Automatic 10–30% traffic spillback to hosted on p95 > 1000ms sustained for 120s.
- Manual rollback plan documented in cutover-runbook.md (attached) — 30-minute rollback target to fully route back to hosted if needed.

Acceptance criteria for go:
- 2 hour mirror at >=80% peak with p95 generation latency within 1.5x of hosted baseline.
- No GPU OOMs and sustained GPU util < 92% during mirror.
- Successful end-to-end request tracing for 100 sampled requests.

Next steps: Karthik will upload the sizing doc to the shared Drive link and I’ll schedule a 30-minute prep call (Nov 12) to walk SpectraWorks infra through the runbook.

Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com
